thread:
Ana M: Heads up — noticed a p99/regress in eu1 on A10 and L4 after the afternoon canary (rollout 4927). p50 fine, but p99 jumped ~2.5x on text-gen workloads.
Liam K: saw that. Is it correlated with batch size or kernel selection? any CI failures?
Ana M: CI perf job flagged a regression on the l4-profile matrix: perf-ci reported +180ms p99 on 512-token tail. Attaching profiling snippet.
perf-ci: `CI: perf/latency-eu1-l4-512 failed (p99 +183ms) — see /artifacts/1998842120`
Sophia R: quick check: KV cache hit rate for canary traces dropped from ~91% to ~64% for the same workload. That smells like cache churn / prefetch mismatch.
Rahul P: Also seeing more small batches (~2-3) rather than expected 8-12 on L4 under same QPS. Batching heuristics might be deciding to flush early due to the new kernel latency estimator change in PR#4972.
Ana M: here's the hot profiling excerpt (from perf agent):
```
kernel_selector: picked kernel=v2_heuristic (latency_est=12.3ms)
seq_len=512 mean_batch=3.1 kv_hit_rate=0.64
network_queue_depth=18 nic_tx_packets_drop=0.02%
cpu_sys: +22% user: +8%
KV cache evict rate: 9.2/s (prev baseline 1.1/s)
```
Liam K: evict rate jumping that much will invalidate prefixes and blow up compute. Could be due to changed slab threshold in L4 allocator from PR 4899? But that PR was supposed to be safe.
Sophia R: bisect started: `git bisect --term-old baseline --term-new HEAD` narrowed to range 4860..4972. Early suspect is 4972 (batch heuristics + kernel selector refactor).
Rahul P: I ran a targeted revert of the kernel selector commit in a local canary — p99 dropped back to near-baseline on the same traffic replay. KV hit rate returned to ~89%.
Ana M: can you paste the exact commit you reverted? we need a safe rollback if this holds.
Rahul P: reverted commit `c7f4a1e` (kernel picker: introduce latency-est multiplier for preference). Test command: `./deploy/canary --cluster eu1 --tag revert-c7f4a1e`
deploy-bot: Canary deployment started: eu1/revert-c7f4a1e @ 1998842325
Sophia R: after canary revert metrics (10m): p99 down 160ms, kv evict rate 1.3/s, mean_batch ~9.2.
Ana M: good. This looks like interplay: the new latency multiplier reduces choice of high-throughput kernels, causing smaller batches, causing more KV thrash and NIC queueing on A10/L4 hardware with our typical request size distribution.
Liam K: action items: 1) hold rollout 4927 in eu1 (and pause further L4/A10 rollouts), 2) revert PR4972 from canary to stable while we redesign kernel selector to include batch-size impact, 3) add unit/regression test that measures kvcache eviction rate under synthetic mixes.
Sophia R: I'll open a follow-up PR with a reduced-impact kernel score that penalizes latency only when it affects throughput less than 5% (w/ perf tests). Also adding a perf CI check: simulate KV cache behavior with sampled prefixes.
Rahul P: I'm updating the incident doc and will post the bisect notes + commands. Putting a rollout hold tag on the PR now.
Ana M: thanks all. If anyone sees eu1 p99 climb again after revert, ping here immediately and we'll roll back globally. :thumbsup:
perf-ci: note: re-run scheduled: perf/latency-eu1-l4-512 @ 1998842680
deploy-bot: Revert canary completed: eu1/revert-c7f4a1e @ 1998842765
Liam K: monitoring — plotting kv_hit_rate, mean_batch, p99 over next 30m. will post a short summary when stable.
Sophia R: summary (post-revert): p99 ~ baseline +8ms, kv_hit_rate 88-91%, mean_batch 8-11. Looks good so far.
Ana M: closing the immediate incident — we'll track the follow-up PR and add a postmortem once the longer replay tests are done. Thanks team. :relieved:
